shouldFix.title: The component-writer repair conflates the writer with the requester and overstates permission-v6 token scope.
evidence: File 04 makes the core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner the SC-OPS sole writer, so the new sentence that components are not SC-OPS writers is correct.

permission-truth-tables.v6 defines PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE over a component's declared class and explicitly distinguishes a HOST-STAGED write from a direct component write; in the former, the host performs and can reverse the write.

The candidate nevertheless says the token's scopeParameter 'therefore resolves to one preview class (SC-CACHE), not two'. A host-staged SC-OPS write still has a host writer, so that conclusion does not follow from the no-component-writer rule.
shouldFix.impact: The recorded DR-105 tension is misstated and could make a cross-class test reject a lawful host-owned SC-OPS write merely because a component requested it.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State that direct component writes may target SC-CACHE only. Keep host-staged or brokered SC-OPS writes distinct as host writes, and route the permission token's requester/actor semantics to DR-105 without declaring its whole scopeParameter single-class.

verdictRule: ACCEPT only when blockers=0 and shouldFix=0.
conclusion: REJECT: the boundedness exception contradicts the formal scope of SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, and the component-writer repair overstates the permission token's class scope by conflating requester with writer.
